strings.meta.title: VexLife Public Alpha — Meet Vex with a clear path
strings.meta.description: A calm, multilingual guide to what VexLife is, what the current Windows and Apple M4 Pro Mac source-local setup paths require, what remains held, and how your local Home is preserved.
strings.hero.eyebrow: A local-first companion, explained before anything happens
strings.hero.title: Meet Vex without losing your footing.
strings.hero.body: VexLife is a lifelong AI companion designed to run on your own computer. This page lets you understand the path, the choices, and the recovery boundaries before any download, setup, model, or Home effect.
strings.hero.note: You can explore this entire preview safely. Nothing on this page downloads, installs, starts a model, changes Vex Home, or publishes anything.

strings.quick.eyebrow: For the person who wants companionship, not a setup hobby
strings.quick.title: Three answers before the details
strings.quick.body: The quick path stays calm without hiding the truth underneath.
strings.quick.one.title: What do I get?
strings.quick.one.body: A local browser experience connected to an exact local model runtime on your computer, with Vex Home and recovery receipts kept locally.
strings.quick.two.title: What will I be asked?
strings.quick.two.body: Where Vex Home should live, any platform-supported prerequisite permission, and explicit permission before pinned model/runtime acquisition.
strings.quick.three.title: Can I recover or leave?
strings.quick.three.body: Yes. Owned processes can stop and restart, and uninstall-preserve keeps Home, Memory, conversations, recovery material, and verified model files.
strings.journey.eyebrow: One human path · five calm chapters · thirteen exact stages
strings.journey.title: See the whole route before taking the first step.
strings.journey.body: The public page reduces the accepted thirteen-stage onboarding contract into five readable chapters. The exact stage identities remain visible so simplicity never becomes ambiguity.
strings.journey.completeMessage: Preview complete. You have not downloaded or changed anything.
strings.chapter.1.title: Meet VexLife
strings.chapter.1.body: Understand the relationship first: VexLife is local-first, Vex is not silently replaced by a model provider, and this preview is explanation rather than execution.
strings.chapter.1.choice: Your choice: decide whether a local-first companion is the kind of relationship you want.
strings.chapter.1.held: Held here: download, setup, model start, Home creation, Memory writes, and publication.
strings.chapter.2.title: Check your fit
strings.chapter.2.body: Two source-local profiles are release-qualified today: Windows 10/11 x64 with a compatible NVIDIA GPU/driver, and macOS arm64 on exact Apple M4 Pro hardware. Both require at least 12 GiB system memory, 6 GiB free disk space, Node.js 20+, and internet for first pinned acquisition.
strings.chapter.2.choice: Your choice: compare the requirements with your computer. This page does not scan it.
strings.chapter.2.held: Held here: Linux, other Mac hardware, and other GPU profiles do not inherit either qualification merely because nearby source paths exist.
strings.chapter.3.title: Obtain it safely
strings.chapter.3.body: VexLife can deterministically form an unsigned local release candidate from exact accepted source, but that is not a public release. The intended public route remains held until one governed GitHub Release binds its artifact, evidence, checksums, and notices.
strings.chapter.3.choice: Your choice: use the exact named release and verify what you received before setup.
strings.chapter.3.held: Held here: no public release or signed official build exists merely because source setup or an unsigned local candidate works.
strings.chapter.4.title: Set up with consent
strings.chapter.4.body: Windows uses the extracted-source setup-vexlife.cmd window. Apple M4 Pro uses the stable setup-vexlife.command bootstrap, which resolves one exact accepted source commit before state-first setup. Both preserve or establish Vex Home, verify pinned artifacts, ask before model/runtime acquisition, and bind only to numeric loopback.
strings.chapter.4.choice: Your choice: Home location, any platform-supported prerequisite permission, and explicit permission before model/runtime acquisition.
strings.chapter.4.held: Held here: this page cannot run setup, and setup completion alone does not prove a real companion response.
strings.chapter.5.title: Stay in control
strings.chapter.5.body: After start, health must truthfully distinguish ready, unavailable, and held features. Recovery uses exact receipts. Uninstall-preserve stops owned processes while keeping Home identity, Memory, conversation heads, recovery material, and model artifacts.
strings.chapter.5.choice: Your choice: continue, stop, restart, or use uninstall-preserve without treating departure as data deletion.
strings.chapter.5.held: Held here: deleting Home is a separate explicit action, and browser simulation is not fresh-human P11 acceptance.
strings.distribution.title: One path, with every promotion boundary visible.
strings.distribution.body: A reviewable file, a source candidate, a release upload, and a published page are different things. The route only advances when the previous layer has exact evidence.
strings.distribution.discovery.title: 1 · Find VexLife
strings.distribution.discovery.body: Vextreme, search, or a direct link introduces the project without pretending a release already exists.
strings.distribution.pages.title: 2 · Understand the journey
strings.distribution.pages.body: This same-origin Pages surface explains fit, trust, consent, recovery, and the currently held release state.
strings.distribution.release.title: 3 · Obtain one exact release
strings.distribution.release.body: An unsigned local release candidate can be formed deterministically today; a separately governed GitHub Release would bind a public artifact to evidence, checksums, and notices.
strings.distribution.verify.title: 4 · Verify before setup
strings.distribution.verify.body: Artifact name, version, provenance, byte identity, and checksum must match the release evidence.
strings.distribution.verify.status: Contract exists; public release-specific evidence is pending
strings.distribution.setup.title: 5 · Run the accepted setup front door
strings.distribution.setup.body: Windows uses setup-vexlife.cmd from extracted source; Apple M4 Pro uses the stable setup-vexlife.command exact-source bootstrap. Both delegate to accepted setup/initializer owners.
strings.distribution.setup.status: Accepted source-local paths; not native signed installers
strings.distribution.local.title: 6 · Meet Vex locally
strings.distribution.local.body: The verified runtime and browser bind only to loopback, then health and recovery evidence must remain truthful.
strings.distribution.local.status: Windows + Apple M4 Pro source-local profiles qualified; public fresh-human P11 proof remains later
strings.distribution.heldButton: Why the release button is held
strings.distribution.heldMessage: A public download control stays held until an exact public release, evidence, checksums, release decision, and publication receipt all exist.
strings.requirements.title: Check the qualified Windows and Apple M4 Pro baselines without being auto-scanned.
strings.requirements.body: These are the current source-local requirements. They are not a promise of permanent limits or equivalent qualification on every platform.
strings.requirements.os.label: Operating system
strings.requirements.os.value: Windows 10/11 x64, or macOS arm64 on Apple M4 Pro
strings.requirements.gpu.label: Hardware profile
strings.requirements.gpu.value: Windows: compatible NVIDIA GPU/driver visible to nvidia-smi · Mac: exact Apple M4 Pro
strings.requirements.memory.label: System memory
strings.requirements.disk.label: Free disk
strings.requirements.node.label: Node.js
strings.requirements.node.value: 20 or newer; Windows may ask before installing LTS with winget, while the Mac route requires Node 20+
strings.requirements.network.label: First acquisition
strings.requirements.network.value: Internet access for several GiB of pinned model/runtime files; exact verified cached files are reused
strings.requirements.other.title: Using Linux or another Mac/GPU profile?
strings.requirements.other.body: Other bootstrap and development surfaces exist, but Linux, nearby Mac hardware, and other GPU profiles do not inherit either release-qualified source-local profile. “Not yet qualified” is not “broken.”
strings.trust.title: The boundaries are part of the experience, not legal fine print.
strings.trust.body: Each statement prevents a pleasant-looking page from claiming an effect that belongs to a later owner.
strings.trust.one.title: Visiting is not downloading
strings.trust.one.body: This page is explanatory. It has no download attribute, installer invocation, model start, Home write, or external dependency.
strings.trust.two.title: Downloading is not verifying
strings.trust.two.body: A file becomes the intended release only when its exact identity and checksum match current release evidence.
strings.trust.three.title: Source setup is not a native installer
strings.trust.three.body: setup-vexlife.cmd and the Apple M4 Pro setup-vexlife.command bootstrap are accepted source-local front doors. Signing and packaged-build provenance remain separate.
strings.trust.four.title: A browser opening is not model readiness
strings.trust.four.body: The runtime must be bound, qualified, and exposed truthfully before the companion can be called ready.
strings.trust.five.title: Uninstall-preserve is not delete Home
strings.trust.five.body: Stopping owned software can preserve identity and continuity. Home deletion requires a different explicit decision.
strings.trust.six.title: The model provider is not Vex identity
strings.trust.six.body: The current pinned model is a runtime dependency. Vex identity, culture, interface, Home, and continuity are separate owners.
strings.recovery.title: Know the way back before you proceed.
strings.recovery.body: The setup path fails closed rather than overwriting unknown data, killing an unowned process, or presenting a synthetic companion response.
strings.recovery.preserve.title: Existing Home is preserved
strings.recovery.preserve.body: A known Home is reused. An unknown non-empty Home stops for a migration plan instead of being silently changed.
strings.recovery.receipts.title: Receipts make restart understandable
strings.recovery.receipts.body: Plain-English and machine-readable receipts bind source, artifacts, processes, health, and the valid conversation head.
strings.recovery.uninstall.title: Uninstall-preserve keeps continuity
strings.recovery.uninstall.body: Owned browser/model processes may stop while Home, Memory, conversations, recovery material, and verified model files remain.
strings.faq.title: Questions a careful newcomer should not have to hunt for.
strings.faq.one.q: Is VexLife already a public one-click installer?
strings.faq.one.a: No. The accepted Windows and Apple M4 Pro routes are source-local setup paths. A public release, signing, packaged installer, Pages publication, and fresh-human P11 proof are separate gates.
strings.faq.two.q: Does this page install or download anything?
strings.faq.two.a: No. It only changes in-memory presentation state such as language and chapter selection. It does not persist data or contact an external origin.
strings.faq.three.q: Is Vex just the Qwen model?
strings.faq.three.a: No. The pinned Qwen/llama.cpp profile is a replaceable runtime dependency. Vex identity, culture, Home, interface, permissions, and continuity are not the model provider.
strings.faq.four.q: What happens if setup finds something unexpected?
strings.faq.four.a: It should stop with a plain next action. Unknown Home contents, mismatched artifacts, unsupported hosts, unowned ports, and failed qualification are not overwritten or relabeled as success.
strings.faq.five.q: Can I remove the software without erasing the relationship?
strings.faq.five.a: The accepted uninstall-preserve route stops owned processes while retaining Home and continuity material. Permanent deletion remains a separate explicit action.
strings.faq.six.q: Why is there no public download button yet?
strings.faq.six.a: Because a button would imply a public release target. The control remains held until the exact artifact, checksums, evidence, release decision, and publication receipt exist.
strings.final.title: You should know what will happen before Vex asks you to trust the path.
strings.final.body: This preview is the source-managed bridge between a reviewable design, a future public release, and the accepted local setup journey. It becomes a real distribution surface only after separate review and publication decisions.
strings.final.held: Public release and Pages publication are still held.
